segments.title: 第61章 絕對音感
segments.content:
Rekindling the Verdant Era Chapter 61: Perfect Pitch

August 27th, afternoon.

The first-year students of Fuyi High School, organized by class and dressed in military training uniforms, filed out of the school gates in long, orderly lines and headed to their respective buses.

As the sports representative, Zhu Yufei carried a red and yellow banner printed with "First Year, Class Eight" and led the way at the front.

Li Luo was at the back of the class, chatting idly with Kong Junxiang as they walked.

Normally, arranging for high school students to go to a military camp for training was a rare privilege, even for some universities.

But the principal of Fuyi High School had a military background, placed great importance on this aspect of student development, and had strong connections, which was how he could arrange for the students to have an experience at a military camp.

Even the neighboring Qianjiang University didn't have this opportunity.

Of course, this was also related to the number of students.

After all, Qianjiang University might have several thousand new students in a single year.

Fuyi High School had just over six hundred first-year students, which was a relatively manageable number.

"What are you looking at, Teacher Kong?" Li Luo asked curiously, glancing at Kong Junxiang's phone.

"Just checking some news." Kong Junxiang silently closed the Qidian Reading App. After confirming that a certain book had just been updated, he felt a slight itch of anticipation and put his phone back in his pocket.

The line was moving slowly, and Zhu Yufei at the front had already led the group onto the bus.

The students were all more or less a little excited, feeling as if they were going on a field trip.

Li Luo followed the line, looked around, and spotted the bus for Class One across the road.

Ying Chanxi was also at the back of her class line. After seeing Li Luo, she waved at him.

But before Li Luo could respond, Yan Zhusheng, who was next to him, also noticed Ying Chanxi's wave and politely waved back.

"She was waving at me," Li Luo said, turning his head.

"Was she?" Yan Zhusheng paused for a moment, then asked, "But I've treated her to a meal, and you haven't. Why couldn't she be waving at me?"

Li Luo: "...You actually make a good point."

After boarding the bus, Li Luo sat next to Yan Zhusheng. Across the aisle were Kong Junxiang and Drill Instructor Zhang.

After everyone had stowed their luggage of various sizes overhead, Lin Yuan couldn't wait to open the guitar case he had brought, holding his guitar and showing it off in his seat.

Although he couldn't sit with Hua Xiuxiu, she was seated right across the aisle, which was still an excellent spot.

The bus hadn't even started moving, but Lin Yuan was already eagerly strumming.

Despite being very nervous during his vocal performance last night, with his fingers trembling after he finished singing,

Lin Yuan's confidence had been partially unleashed after he had time to process it.

At least now, singing in front of his classmates no longer made him as nervous as when he first introduced himself at the beginning of the school year.

Li Luo hadn't brought his guitar this time.

After all, once he knew the price of the guitar, he felt a little embarrassed to be rough with it. He would just play it at home to scratch the itch, and wouldn't bring it out unless necessary.

It just so happened that Lin Yuan had brought his. After the bus started moving, Lin Yuan played for about ten minutes and was finally getting a bit tired.

Li Luo, in the front row, beckoned for it.

He wasn't any kind of guitar master. To him, any guitar felt more or less the same—as long as it could be played. At most, he could feel some difference in the feel and sound quality.

"Alright, alright, taking requests." After confirming the bus was on the highway and relatively stable, Li Luo stood up, leaned against the aisle railing, and said to the class with a smile, "Let's all sing together."

"Let us row our oars~"

"The little boat pushes through the waves~"

Almost everyone knew how to hum a line or two of this song. As Li Luo started the tune, a few of the bolder students began to sing along. Gradually, the entire bus of students was swept up, singing together:

"The sea reflects the beautiful white pagoda~"

"Surrounded by green trees and red walls~"

Listening to the singing on the bus, Drill Instructor Zhang, who was sitting to the side, couldn't help but chuckle. "You guys are making this military training seem like a spring outing."

Kong Junxiang smiled too. He glanced at Li Luo, who was enthusiastically playing the guitar nearby, and felt the lively and cheerful atmosphere among the students in the class, becoming even more satisfied.

The military training had only been going on for two or three days, but thanks to Li Luo, most of the students in the class already felt a strong sense of belonging to Class Eight.

This was exactly one of the goals the school had hoped to achieve by arranging military training at the start of the school year.

Often, whether a class was good or not depended not only on the teacher and the school, but also on the overall atmosphere of the class.

Someone like Li Luo, who could unite all of Class Eight in just a few short days, had saved Kong Junxiang a lot of trouble.

"Teacher Kong, you should sing a song too."

Just as Kong Junxiang was smiling and watching the scene, Li Luo had already set his sights on him and moved closer with a grin.

Kong Junxiang had actually only graduated from university a few years ago, so he quickly blended in with everyone.

Li Luo only stopped playing the guitar after everyone was tired of singing.

He was about to hand the guitar back when Yan Zhusheng suddenly grabbed his arm and took the guitar from him.

"What's wrong?" Li Luo asked, puzzled. "You want to sing yourself?"

Yan Zhusheng hadn't opened her mouth during the group sing-along, and Li Luo had thought it was because his playing was bad and she wasn't interested.

But Yan Zhusheng just said, "I'm tuning it."

Holding the guitar, she gently plucked a string, listened intently with her ear cocked, and then turned the tuning peg to adjust the string's tension.

"Is this guitar out of tune?" Li Luo asked curiously.

Yan Zhusheng glanced at him, then said, "It's a complete mess. The rhythm it produces sounds like noise."

Li Luo's mouth twitched. "...Your ears are a bit spoiled."

"There." Yan Zhusheng finished tuning and handed it back to Li Luo. "You can try it now."

Li Luo took the guitar, half-convinced, and tried strumming the strings.

Then he couldn't help but raise his eyebrows.

How should he put it... the feeling was very strange.

He had found the tone and quality acceptable when he was playing earlier, but after Yan Zhusheng's adjustments, the sound did seem to be much better.

"How did you change it?" Li Luo turned his head and asked.

"First, determine the correct pitch of one string, then adjust the others in sequence, that's all," Yan Zhusheng said very simply.

"What if all six strings are out of tune?"

"Then just tune one of them first."

"How do you know the tuned note is correct?"

Yan Zhusheng gave him a strange look. "My ears tell me."

"...That's called perfect pitch, right?"

"I suppose so."

Li Luo smacked his lips, then something suddenly occurred to him, and he asked, "Can perfect pitch be trained?"

"No." Yan Zhusheng shook her head. "But with a lot of practice, you can get close to the effect of perfect pitch."

Li Luo thought of his memory palace, which could even replicate and remember sounds. If he wanted to, could he also achieve the effect of perfect pitch?

"Hey, let me try too." At this thought, Li Luo pushed the guitar into Yan Zhusheng's hands. "Scramble the tuning, then teach me how to tune it."

Yan Zhusheng blinked, looking down at the guitar in her hands. "For an ordinary person to tune a guitar, it's best to use a tuner."
